what: Kernel #1 bandwidth pass 2: uint32 vector loads, wide tiles, CUDA graphs
result: REGRESSION. Pass 2 is slower than pass 1 and the cause is measurement variance, not just the code.

cuda_graph.verdict: graph replay is SLOWER than eager; launch overhead is not the dominant cost at this tile size, so graphing adds nothing and costs a copy

smoking_gun_for_variance: In the same run, the N=1 sweep measured 1.9595 ms for tile bn=32/bk=128/w=1, then the curve section re-measured the identical configuration at 3.9541 ms. A 2x spread on the same kernel, same tile, same process. Any single measurement on a shared T4 is therefore unreliable at the 2x level.
what_this_means: The pass 1 number of 24.6 GB/s should also be treated as one sample, not a stable figure, until it is a median of repeated runs.
CUDA graph replay is negative here and should be dropped from the plan for now.
The uint32 vector-load change cannot be evaluated from this run because the noise band is wider than the effect being measured.
action: Pass 3 must fix the harness before touching the kernel: warm-up, many iterations, median and spread over 5 separate launches rather than one, and report p10/p50/p90. Only numbers with a spread under 20 percent are usable for a claim.
verdict: Pass 2 did not improve bandwidth. Reported as a failure rather than smoothed away. No bandwidth claim is being made from this run.
